Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the CloudForge Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to register by pressing star one one on your telephone keypad. Please be advised that today's call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to CloudForge's Q2 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Sarah Chen, CEO; Mike Patel, CFO; Lisa Wong, CTO; and David Kim, Chief Revenue Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of federal securities laws. Actual results may differ materially due to various risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings, including our most recent 10-Q and 10-K, for a complete discussion of these factors.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm pleased to report on CloudForge's performance for Q2 2024. We achieved significant milestones this quarter, driven by strong demand for our CloudForge AI platform and continued execution of our strategic initiatives.

Our focus this quarter was on five key areas: advancing our product roadmap, evolving our customer mix, expanding gross margins, strengthening our cash position, and updating our full-year guidance.

Let me start with our product roadmap. I'm thrilled to share the momentum across our platform at CloudForge, where we're the leading SaaS provider of AI-powered workflow automation and collaboration software, serving thousands of enterprise customers globally, including a substantial portion of the Fortune 100. Our roadmap centers on three pillars: speeding up AI adoption to fuel ARR growth, improving our composable architecture for quicker time-to-value, and targeting high-growth verticals with customized solutions.

On AI and generative AI integrations—our primary driver of net revenue retention, which reached impressive levels this quarter—we've experienced rapid uptake of CloudForge AI Insights, our native AI copilot now integrated throughout our stack. Since introducing the latest version earlier this year, we've added numerous new agents, including tools for predictive analytics that leverage advanced language models to process data from emails, meetings, and team communications, improving forecast precision by over 30% for initial users like major financial institutions. Usage metrics are outstanding: a majority of our largest customers engage with these AI features daily, contributing to substantial year-over-year growth in AI-related ARR. Coming up in the second half, we'll launch a low-code builder allowing customers to create tailored agents using models from key partners, with early tests showing dramatically faster deployment times compared to competitors.

Next, our composable architecture is transforming how enterprises handle workflows. We've transitioned to an API-first, event-driven foundation using streaming technologies and federated queries, enabling seamless integrations that cut development time significantly. A key highlight is our new orchestration marketplace, similar to leading industry hubs, now featuring hundreds of partner applications from data providers and marketing tools. This has led to sharp increases in transactions and larger average deal values. Ahead, we're introducing a visual workflow designer with standards-compliant support and built-in security protocols, which internal tests indicate can accelerate processes fivefold; we've already lined up commitments from numerous early users aiming for high attachment in new sales.

Regionally, we're customizing the roadmap to local opportunities. In North America, our core market driving over half of ARR, we're pushing mid-market growth with an accessible pricing tier that includes lighter AI capabilities, fueling strong customer gains. EMEA has accelerated thanks to data sovereignty features; we're rolling out a specialized solution for financial services with regulatory compliance next month to deepen banking penetration. APAC is surging with mobile optimizations and edge computing for reliable performance, gaining traction with large telcos and consultancies, while partnerships open doors in key markets like Japan and China for localized AI.

These efforts create a strong competitive edge through data networks and partner ecosystems. Processing billions of events yearly builds exclusive datasets for our AI, outpacing rivals in scale and accuracy. Expansion remains strong, with low churn among AI users, and we're on track for significant ARR growth, with a large share from new AI modules, exceeding broader market trends.

Mike will cover the customer mix, margins, cash, and guidance in more detail. Overall, we're confident in sustaining this momentum to create long-term shareholder value.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike Patel to discuss the financials.

Mike Patel:
Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah highlighted, we delivered a strong quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $112 million, representing a 26% increase year-over-year. Our non-GAAP gross margin was 78.5%, and non-GAAP operating income was $25 million.

Turning to gross margin performance, which highlights the power of our scalable SaaS model. For Q2 fiscal 2024, we achieved a non-GAAP gross margin of 78.5%, an improvement of 130 basis points from 77.2% in Q1 and 240 basis points from 76.1% in Q2 last year. GAAP gross margin came in at 77.8%, up from 76.5% last quarter and 75.4% a year ago. These gains reflect operational leverage as we grow, supported by our efficient multi-tenant setup.

Key factors included cost of revenue dropping to 21.5% of total revenue, down from 22.8% sequentially and 23.9% year-over-year. Hosting and infrastructure, about 60% of costs, saw efficiencies from major cloud providers like AWS and Google Cloud. With average seats up 18% to 2.1 million active users, we secured better terms on commitments, lowering per-unit storage and compute by around 12% quarter-over-quarter—much like gains seen by peers scaling on hyperscalers.

We also advanced efficiencies in support and services. Our AI self-service tools now handle 45% of basic tickets independently, up from 32% last year, reducing support as a percentage of revenue to 3.7% from 4.2%, while keeping gross retention at 98.5%. Lower-margin services fell to 8% of revenue from 11%, as more customers adopt streamlined enterprise onboarding.

By region, North America at 62% of revenue hit 80.2% margins—our best yet—from big deployments in finance and healthcare. EMEA improved 350 basis points to 76.8% with our new Frankfurt center cutting costs and meeting regulations, lifting NRR to 112%. APAC held at 74.5%, but Sydney investments target upside from 25% seat growth in manufacturing.

This positions us well, with dollar net expansion at 118% from high-margin AI upsells and optimizations like auto-scaling that trimmed idle costs by 8%. We guide Q3 margins to 78.8%-79.3%, heading to low-80s next year with AI acceleration and a $50 million infrastructure program. We're monitoring AI energy costs, offset by our cloud mix and agreements. This supports a Rule of 40 score near 48, funding 14% R&D spend and our first $100 million buyback.

Next, on customer mix trends between enterprise and SMB, which is crucial for balanced growth in this environment. Enterprise—ACV over $100K, mainly large globals—now makes up 48% of ARR, up from 42% last year and 45% last quarter, thanks to 28% logo growth to 320 accounts. SMB—under $100K—holds 52%, but new logos grew 12% to about 28,500. This shift added 150 basis points to our ARR growth.

Cohorts show enterprise adding $42 million new ACV at $162K average, SMB $28 million at $6.8K. Enterprise NRR at 118% with strong expansions, SMB 108% with offset churn. Enterprise gains stem from AI features like our intelligence layer integrating with major stacks, boosting deal sizes 25% in regulated sectors, including multi-region bank wins.

SMB stabilized after pricing updates to $29/user tiers, strong via marketplaces but softer in high-rate times. North America dominates enterprise at 62%, EMEA up to 22%, APAC at 16% but growing fast. We're aiming for 55% enterprise by year-end via dedicated sales, product expansions—62% of enterprise ARR from upsells—and SMB flywheels, with pipeline efficiency high despite longer cycles.

Now, our liquidity and cash runway remain top-tier, enabling strategy execution amid caution. Cash, equivalents, and short-term investments ended Q2 at $452 million, up 12% from Q1's $403 million, fueled by $68 million operating cash flow—our eighth straight positive quarter—at 28% margin, up from 22% year-over-year. This ties to 84% gross margins, DSO at 52 days, and OpEx discipline for a Rule of 40 of 58.

Uses included $22 million capex for AI data centers, akin to peers' consumption builds, supporting NRR uplift from new agents. We repurchased $15 million in shares, 1.2 million at $145 average, 2% of float—no debt. Net burn was minimal $12 million, annualizing under $50 million, for over 36 months runway at current growth, indefinite at FCF midpoint of $220-250 million or 18-20% margins.

U.S. generated most at 65% ARR, EMEA 22%, APAC 13% with collections ramps. Priorities: AI efficiencies cutting churn to 4.2% and 135% NRR; GTM with 14-month CAC payback; M&A with dry powder. Q3 CFO $75-85 million expected.

Finally, on full-year FY24 revenue guidance: With Q1 at $105 million up 24%, Q2 $112 million up 26%, H1 $217 million ahead of plan, we're raising and narrowing to $478 million to $484 million, or 25.8%-27.4% growth over FY23's $380 million. Subscriptions ~$460-466 million, 96% mix.

ARR ended Q2 at $465 million, up 27% and $15 million above plan, guiding to $480-485 million end-year with Q4 adds $12-14 million, from expansions in top customers. NRR at 116%, ahead of target, driven by AI modules at 40% attach and 15% ACV lift; eight $5 million+ deals, like a $7.2 million Fortune 50 expansion.

Balanced regionally: Americas 68% at 26%, EMEA 28%, APAC 22% accelerating. AI tailwinds, pricing tests at 8-10%, offset by macro delays, forex. Rule of 40 at 85% in Q2, pipeline 3.2x.

We continue investing in R&D for innovation. Cash remains strong at $452 million, with flexibility for growth.

I'll now turn the call over to Lisa for a technology update.

Lisa Wong:
Thank you, Mike. This quarter, we advanced our AI capabilities, deeply embedding them into our core platform. Adoption of AI-powered features is surging, boosting engagement and outcomes. We've prioritized platform security and scalability for enterprise needs, including hyperscaler optimizations and AI self-service that resolve more tickets autonomously while upholding 99.99% uptime.

Now, I'll turn the call back to the operator for Q&A.

Operator:
Thank you. To ask a question, press star one one. Our first question comes from Ben Thompson with Piper Sandler.

Ben Thompson:
Hi, good afternoon. Can you discuss the impact of CloudForge AI on your overall growth, and what kind of attach rates are you seeing with it?

David Kim:
Thanks, Ben. CloudForge AI has been transformative for growth, contributing to our 116% NRR through upsells like Insights and agents that deliver 15% ACV uplift. It's central to eight multi-million deals this half, including expansions to full operations. Attach rates hit 40% in new enterprise wins, with daily usage over 60% in top cohorts, driving 45% YoY AI ARR growth and positioning us for 20%+ attachment on logos.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Rachel Kim with Barclays.

Rachel Kim:
What are your plans for international expansion, specifically in the APAC region?

Sarah Chen:
Great question, Rachel. APAC is a priority, with 22% growth this year ramping to 30%+ in H2. We've invested in Sydney and Tokyo nodes for low latency, securing deals with top Japanese banks via localized models. Mobile enhancements and edge computing boost engagement 50%, while Alibaba partnerships target China. EMEA data centers similarly fuel 28% growth—expect continued acceleration as AI resonates regionally.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Jordan Patel with RBC Capital.

Jordan Patel:
How are you managing churn in the current economic environment, and what's the trend you are seeing in NRR?

Mike Patel:
Thanks, Jordan. Churn is well-controlled at 4.5% gross dollar retention, elite versus peers, thanks to AI features like predictive models dropping voluntary churn to 4.2%. Self-service resolves 45% tickets, and sticky expansions keep NRR trending at 116% through Q2, up from prior targets, with enterprise at 118%. SMB at 108%, but flywheels and pricing discipline sustain 105-110% outlook despite macro pressures.

Operator:
Thank you. I'm showing no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Sarah Chen for closing remarks.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you for joining us today. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain committed to delivering strong results for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again on our next earnings call.

Operator:
Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
